newsitem.title: USA: US corp bond players eye next week's new issues.
newsitem.headline: US corp bond players eye next week's new issues.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond players were looking forward to next week's business on Thursday as new issuance for the current week seemed to have temporarily run out of steam, syndicate sources said.

"Many issuers rushed to price new deals over the past couple of days, thinking this was a technical bounce (in interest rates) and that the market would erode from here," an investment grade sydnicate source said.
Corporations sold $2.5 billion in new bonds so far this week. Syndicate officials said this was a "healthy" amount, but still lower than supply in previous weeks.

Investment-grade market players were already talking about a $1 billion 144a private placement offering from Comcast Cable Communications Inc, a unit of Comcast Corp, via a Goldman Sachs & Co-led syndicate.
The offering, scheduled for next week, is expected to consist of seven- 10-, 20- and 30-year securities. The 30-year tranche is expected to have a 12-year put, sources said.
Standard & Poor's has rated the proposed issue BBB-minus.
Tenaga Nasional Berhad, a Malaysian utility, may also sell $400 million to $500 milllion in 10-year notes via UBS Securities and Credit Suisse First Boston next week.

Market players said SK Telecom Co Ltd, South Korea's largest cellular phone and radio paging company, may also sell $230 million in 10-year notes via Morgan Stanley & Co next week, market sources said.

Market players said many emerging market companies are still attracted to current interest rates in the U.S., despite the recent rise which has discouraged some domestic issuers from tapping the market.
In the high-yield market, Exide Holdings Europe SA 150 million mark offering was the only deal expected for the remainder of the week.
The offering, being marketed simultaneously in the U.S. and Europe, is one of the first mark-denominated junk bond deals. Morgan Stanley is the lead underwriter.
Price talk on the senior notes, rated B1/B, is 375 basis points to 400 basis points over the seven-year bund.
New junk bond issuance may continue to be light next week as issuers and dealers conduct roadshows, market players said.
New supply was particularly light this week as most investors attended industry conferences hosted by Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette Securities Corp and Bear Stearns & Co Inc.
